what_happened: K0, K1, K2 (first install verified, 0 processes), K3 (second install at %LOCALAPPDATA%\JARVIS-restore installed and verified, 07:29:40Z by host file time) PASS. K4 (dry run of the shipped switch_over.py on the backup) had not finished after more than ten minutes; in both rehearsals it took about one second. No K4 record, no SUMMARY.json. Nothing was imported: the dry run changes nothing and K5 was not reached.
cause: FINAL's recovery.verify() checks the database by extracting it into a temporary folder created beside the archive: tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=Path(archive).parent). The guest script passes the archive on the recovery disc (E:\, read-only). On Windows, Python 3.12.10's tempfile.mkdtemp() treats PermissionError as a name collision and tries the next name whenever the parent is an existing directory for which os.access(W_OK) is true (always true for directories on Windows), up to TMP_MAX = 2,147,483,647 attempts: in effect it never returns.
how_established: code reading (recovery.py at 60d406f; tools/guest/Invoke-Gate18.ps1 K4) and a test on the host with the FINAL package's Python: a write-protect error (winerror 19) is a PermissionError, and mkdtemp was still retrying after 20,000 refused attempts when the test stopped it. Not observed directly inside the VM; the timing (1 s in rehearsal, more than 10 minutes in the VM) is consistent with it.
why_not_found_in_rehearsal: both rehearsals used a writable folder as the 'disc'; the disc build and a real read-only disc could not be rehearsed by Claude.
classification: Gate 18 tooling gap: the guest script must restore from a copy of the backup in a writable folder, not directly from the read-only disc.

Product limitation of FINAL 1.0.11 (found, not fixed: no source change until cutover): verifying or importing a backup that lies on read-only media hangs instead of failing with a message. It does not affect a backup in a normal folder (the cutover case). To be listed for the owner at Gate 20 and fixed in the first release after cutover.
